A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

six3 and otexpression patterns in W. argentaecorrelate to a role in anterior‐posterial axis formation in the LCA of bilaterians but do not provide evidence for a head in the LCA, and otx expression patterns do not provide support for the hypothesis that the prototrocha of the LCA was segmented or that the prototrocopharyngeal region of the LCA corresponded to the head.

the expression of otx in prototroch cells and six3 in cells of the apical organ is an ancestral feature of bilaterians, whereas expression of otx and six3 in the developing CNS is a more derived trait.

the expression of otx and six3 in W. argenta supports a role for these transcription factors in anterior‐posteriop patterning in bilaterian animals but not necessarily in patterning of the head and brain, which are absent in aplacophorans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
six3 and oxt are expressed in a conserved anterior‐posterior pattern in bilaterians and that their expression in the CNS is likely ancestral.

the expression patterns of six3 and/or otx in the CNS are highly variable among protostomes, suggesting that the ancestral role of these genes in CNS patterning is not necessarily the one seen in deuterostomes.

the expression patterns of six3 and/or otx in the protostome‐deuterostome LCA are not well‐understood, and more work is needed to resolve the question of whether or not these genes are involved in the patterning of a head and/or brain in the LCA of bilaterians.
